date.label: Undated narrative of the Gibeonite deception
date.note: Biblical narrative chronology is not independently established as an absolute BCE date.

claims.claim: Gibeonites claim to originate from distant country (Joshua 9:3–13)
Israel’s leaders bind themselves by oath without consulting YHWH (Joshua 9:14–21)
Gibeonites become woodcutters and water drawers (Joshua 9:22–27)
El-Jib is strongly identified with ancient Gibeon through inscribed jar handles bearing its name and associated excavation discoveries; these finds do not prove Joshua 9. (Joshua 9:3)
claims.evidence: Penn Today (2018), paras 3–4; Penn Museum el-Jib object records; Pritchard monographs 1959/1962 (not directly examined).

claims.claim: 2 Samuel 21 explicitly recalls sworn protection of Gibeonites (2 Samuel 21:1–9)

connections.note: Deuteronomy 20:10–18 distinguishes treaty offers made to distant cities from the policy for nearby cities, and that distinction frames the Gibeonites' deception.
Deuteronomy 7:1–6 forbids covenants with the Canaanite peoples, and that prohibition sharpens the dilemma created by the oath sworn to the Gibeonites.
2 Samuel 21:1–9 refers back to a Gibeonite oath in a later narrative, but it does not independently corroborate the Joshua 9 event.
The assault on Gibeon in Joshua 10:1–7 follows immediately from the alliance, as the kings attack Gibeon because it made peace with Israel.
